Arizona Charter Bus Company

Scottsdale Sprinters is an Arizona charter bus company based in Scottsdale, chartering chauffeured coaches by the hour across the Valley and out to Sedona and the Grand Canyon. Its coaches seat 20 to 56 riders. Current published rates run $185–$325 an hour, each on its own minimum, so a charter starts at $740 before tax and $1,625 in the 56-Passenger Motorcoach. Arizona sales tax of 8% is added at checkout and a 50% deposit holds the date.

Last updated: September 18, 2026

What does an Arizona charter bus company actually rent you?

A charter is the whole coach with a professional chauffeur for a block of booked hours — not a seat on a schedule, and not a self-drive rental. Scottsdale Sprinters books coach-class vehicles from one Scottsdale reservations desk, including the Mini Bus (24 Pax), the Executive Mini Bus — Grech (27 Pax), the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) and the 56-Passenger Motorcoach. Every one is a proper-seat vehicle: forward-facing coach seating, a centre aisle, stowed luggage and a chauffeur who stays with the group for the hours you reserved. There is no self-drive or unchauffeured rental in the catalog, so the chauffeur is part of the vehicle rather than an extra you can decline. Reserving the vehicle rather than the seat is what keeps the arithmetic simple: the published hourly rate times billable hours, floored at that vehicle's own minimum. Headcount does not move the total, so 20 riders and 24 riders pay the same for the same Mini Bus (24 Pax).

Which coaches does the fleet run, and what does each one hold?

Seats and bags, vehicle by vehicle: the Mini Bus (24 Pax) seats 24; the Executive Mini Bus — Grech (27 Pax) seats 27 with room for 40 bags; the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) seats 29 with room for 30 bags; the 56-Passenger Motorcoach seats 56 with room for 125 bags. The Mini Bus (24 Pax) carries no published bag count, so its luggage fit is confirmed in writing with the quote rather than assumed. The number inside that unit's internal identifier is a retained legacy reference; the canonical seat count is 24. Seats and bags are separate limits — a group with checked luggage can outgrow a coach it fits by headcount — so confirm both, and any accessibility need, with the reservations team. Above 56 riders the answer is more than one coach rather than a bigger one: two vehicles quoted separately, the totals added, one reservations contact for the whole movement.

What does it cost to charter a bus in Arizona?

The current published hourly rates for the coach class are $185–$325, each vehicle on its own minimum, so the starting total before tax is the rate times that minimum: $740 for the Mini Bus (24 Pax), $900 for the Executive Mini Bus — Grech (27 Pax), $900 for the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax), and $1,625 for the 56-Passenger Motorcoach on its 5-hour minimum. Minimums differ by vehicle: the Mini Bus (24 Pax), the Executive Mini Bus — Grech (27 Pax) and the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) each hold a 4-hour minimum. Hours beyond the minimum bill at the same published hourly rate rather than a penalty rate, and Arizona sales tax of 8% is the only thing added to the fare at checkout — no booking fee, no service charge, no fuel surcharge. A one-way move with no block of hours is a transfer instead, flat within 15 road miles from pickup to drop-off and priced from the drive beyond that, with the empty return included: $450 in the Mini Bus (24 Pax), $550 in the Executive Mini Bus — Grech (27 Pax) and the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax), and $1,250 in the 56-Passenger Motorcoach. Availability varies by date; request a current quote.

What does a coach work out to per seat?

Split evenly across every seat, the starting total is about $31 a head on the Mini Bus (24 Pax), $33 on the Executive Mini Bus — Grech (27 Pax), $31 on the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) and $29 on the 56-Passenger Motorcoach at full capacity. Per-seat figures are an illustration, never a price: you reserve the vehicle and pay its hourly rate, and nobody is billed by the seat. They settle one decision — whether one larger coach beats two smaller ones for the same group. The 5-hour table below prints the same split at a longer day.

Where do Arizona charter trips go?

Two shapes of trip. Inside the metro the coaches work across Scottsdale, Phoenix, Paradise Valley, Tempe, Mesa, Chandler, Gilbert, Glendale, Cave Creek and San Tan Valley, each of which has its own service-area page. Beyond it, the published long-distance days are Sedona and the red rocks, the Grand Canyon South Rim, and Verde Valley wine country. Airport work runs through Phoenix Sky Harbor and Phoenix-Mesa Gateway, each with its own group transfer page. Distance is not billed separately on an hourly charter, so give every address when you book and the driving time between them sits inside the hours you reserved. A long-distance day is the clearest case for a coach: one vehicle, one chauffeur, everyone arriving together, luggage stowed rather than carried. Price it as hours rather than as a transfer, because the coach stays with the group all day.

What do groups charter a coach for?

Five recurring jobs: corporate movements and employee shuttles, conference and convention transfers, wedding guest shuttles, sports and game-day groups, and full-day tours. Each has its own page and its own booking path, linked at the foot of this guide. Corporate and convention work is the most common reason a group charters a coach — a repeating loop across a multi-day programme, or one movement out and back. The corporate transportation and executive minibus group shuttle pages both price the coach class for it. Wedding guest shuttles, sports groups and tour days behave the same way: the coach stays with the group, so the hours are the product rather than the trip. Scottsdale-specific charter questions, including the smaller executive Sprinters that sit below the coach floor, are answered on the Scottsdale charter bus rental guide.

How do you compare Arizona charter bus companies?

Five things settle it, and every one is answerable before you pay a deposit. First, a written quote: the total in writing with the tax shown separately, not a range over the phone. Second, the named vehicle — a quote that says "a coach" is not a quote. It should name the unit, the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) say, so you know what pulls up. Third, capacity and luggage together rather than seats alone. Fourth, the minimum hours: a lower hourly rate on a longer minimum can cost more than a higher rate on a shorter one, so compare starting totals rather than rates. On this fleet that is $740 against $1,625, not $185 against $325. Fifth, what the rate includes — whether the chauffeur, fuel and tolls sit inside the hourly rate or are added afterwards. Ask every company the same five questions and the quotes become comparable.

What is included in the hourly rate?

Included: a professional chauffeur, the reserved coach for the booked hours, fuel and tolls, your itinerary's stops, and bottled water on board. Added at checkout: Arizona sales tax of 8%, the 50% deposit and optional gratuity, never added for you. Outside the rate: parking or venue access billed directly, event permits, meals. Three house rules carry a fee: $1,500 for smoking or vaping, $450 to deep-clean an excessive spill and $450 for a biohazard clean; an added stop on a transfer is $50. Minor spills are not charged.

How do you reserve an Arizona charter coach?

Four steps: pick the coach and the hours, request a current quote with your date and itinerary, confirm with a 50% deposit, and the balance is charged to the card on file 48 hours before pickup. Call or text (623) 986-6339, or email reservations@scottsdalesprinters.com. A quote needs the date, the pickup and final drop addresses, every stop between them, the real headcount, the luggage and the vehicle. The pricing page carries the availability check; the policies page carries the deposit and cancellation tiers in full. Availability is point-in-time until the deposit creates the hold, so check availability and request a current quote rather than working from a figure on a page.

Frequently asked questions

What is an Arizona charter bus company?

A charter bus company rents the whole coach with a professional chauffeur for a block of booked hours rather than selling seats on a schedule. Scottsdale Sprinters is an Arizona charter bus company based in Scottsdale, running coach-class vehicles for groups of 20 to 56 riders.

How much does it cost to charter a bus in Arizona?

Scottsdale Sprinters publishes coach rates of $185–$325 an hour, each vehicle on its own minimum. The Mini Bus (24 Pax) is $185 per hour on a 4-hour minimum, so a charter starts at $740 before tax. The 56-Passenger Motorcoach is $325 per hour on a 5-hour minimum, starting at $1,625. Arizona sales tax of 8% is added at checkout.

How many passengers fit on your Arizona coaches?

At Scottsdale Sprinters, the Mini Bus (24 Pax) seats 24. The Executive Mini Bus — Grech (27 Pax) seats 27. The Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) seats 29. The 56-Passenger Motorcoach seats 56. Larger groups are quoted as more than one coach, and seated capacity is a planning limit — confirm luggage and accessibility separately.

Where in Arizona do your charters go?

Scottsdale Sprinters charters run across Scottsdale, Phoenix, Paradise Valley, Tempe, Mesa, Chandler, Gilbert, Glendale, Cave Creek and San Tan Valley, and out of the metro for Sedona, Grand Canyon South Rim and Verde Valley wine country day trips. Airport work runs through Phoenix Sky Harbor and Phoenix-Mesa Gateway.

Is a chauffeur included, or can we drive the bus ourselves?

A professional chauffeur is included in every Scottsdale Sprinters hourly rate, along with the coach for the booked hours, fuel and tolls, the stops on your itinerary and bottled water on board. There is no self-drive or unchauffeured rental in the catalog. Gratuity is optional and never added for you.

Is there a minimum number of hours?

Yes. At Scottsdale Sprinters, the Mini Bus (24 Pax), the Executive Mini Bus — Grech (27 Pax) and the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) each hold a 4-hour minimum. The 56-Passenger Motorcoach holds a 5-hour minimum. The fare is the published hourly rate times billable hours, never below that floor.

What does the hourly rate include?

On a Scottsdale Sprinters charter the hourly rate covers the chauffeur, the coach for the booked hours, fuel and tolls, the stops on your itinerary and bottled water on board. Arizona sales tax of 8% is added at checkout, and there is no booking fee, service charge or fuel surcharge on the base fare.

Do I pay a deposit, and when is the balance due?

A 50% deposit confirms a Scottsdale Sprinters reservation. The remaining balance is charged automatically to the card on file 48 hours before pickup, and the policies page carries the cancellation tiers in full.

Can we book a one-way group transfer instead of hourly?

Yes. Scottsdale Sprinters prices a one-way group move as a transfer: $450 in the Mini Bus (24 Pax), $550 in the Executive Mini Bus — Grech (27 Pax) and the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax), and $1,250 in the 56-Passenger Motorcoach. Say it is one-way when you request the quote.

How do I get a quote from an Arizona charter bus company?

Check availability and request a current quote on the Scottsdale Sprinters pricing page with your date, vehicle and trip details, or call or text (623) 986-6339 or email reservations@scottsdalesprinters.com. A 50% deposit holds the date.
